1 · What changed

Improvement #1

Revise the action space

Discrete buy/sell → continuous target position a_t ∈ [-1, 1]. The agent sizes exposure continuously (RL-based position management) instead of flipping all-in / all-out.

Improvement #2

Upgrade the state space

Four trend-aware features injected into the observation:

  • SMA-20 slope — Rolling slope of the 20-day moving average -> trend direction.
  • Bollinger width — Normalized band width -> volatility / trend-strength regime.
  • ADX — Average Directional Index -> raw trend strength, direction-agnostic.
  • MACD cross — Golden/death-cross regime -> rule-based trading prior.
Improvement #3

Enhance performance indicators

Max Drawdown, Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, win rate and turnover are computed per episode and reported in the table below.

5 · How each agent traded

Target position vs price (top), equity curve (middle), and drawdown (bottom) for each continuous agent on one deterministic test episode.

6 · Takeaways

  • Trend features improved PPO: return +3.04%, Sharpe +0.72, max drawdown -2.70pp.
  • Trend features did not help SAC: return -7.60%, Sharpe -1.93, max drawdown +1.14pp.
  • The continuous action space turns binary buy/sell into graded position sizing, and the risk metrics (Sharpe, Sortino, Max DD, Calmar) are now first-class outputs rather than post-hoc guesses.
  • Honest context: the 2024–2026 test window was a strong bull market (Buy & Hold +39.10%), so every learned agent trails passive holding here; the value shown is the methodology and the isolated per-algorithm effect, on a single seed.

Which RL algorithm suits position management?

Selecting the RL algorithm for the trend-aware continuous position-management env: SAC vs TD3 vs PPO, same 50,000-step budget each. SAC is the off-policy, max-entropy fit for noisy, data-scarce continuous control.
